30675-presbyterian-worship-its-spirit-me.title: History
30675-presbyterian-worship-its-spirit-me.creator: Unknown
30675-presbyterian-worship-its-spirit-me.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Johnston brings to his task ripe scholarship, including extensive knowledge of Church history and ecclesiology, his proficiency in which he has recently vindicated in such a manner as to leave no room for doubt. To this he adds the teaching of pastoral experience in mission fields, prior to his ordination, and, since then, in large and influential congregations; and, to crown the whole, heartfelt devotion to the Church of his fathers, and unswerving personal loyalty to its King and Head.

arxiv-2212-00477.title: CUNI Non-Autoregressive System for the WMT 22 Efficient Translation Shared Task
arxiv-2212-00477.creator: Jindřich Helcl
arxiv-2212-00477.description: Abstract We present a non-autoregressive system submission to the WMT 22 Efficient Translation Shared Task. Our system was used by Helcl et al. 2022 in an attempt to provide fair comparison between non-autoregressive and autoregressive models. This submission is an effort to establish solid baselines along with sound evaluation methodology, particularly in terms of measuring the decoding speed.

arxiv-2301-13098.title: CHeart: A Conditional Spatio-Temporal Generative Model for Cardiac Anatomy
arxiv-2301-13098.creator: Mengyun Qiao, Shuo Wang, Huaqi Qiu, Antonio de Marvao, Declan P. O’Regan, Daniel Rueckert, Wenjia Bai
arxiv-2301-13098.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mengyun Qiao, Shuo Wang, Huaqi Qiu, Antonio de Marvao, Declan P. O’Regan, Daniel Rueckert, Wenjia Bai. Two key questions in cardiac image analysis are to assess the anatomy and motion of the heart from images; and to understand how they are associated with non-imaging clinical factors such as gender, age and diseases. While the first question can often be addressed by image segmentation and motion tracking algorithms, our capability to model and answer the second question is still limited.

arxiv-2404-18945.title: Advanced analysis of single-molecule spectroscopic data
arxiv-2404-18945.creator: Joshua L. Botha, Bertus van Heerden, Tjaart P.J. Krüger
arxiv-2404-18945.description: Abstract We present Full SMS , a multipurpose graphical user interface (GUI)-based software package for analysing single-molecule spectroscopy (SMS) data. SMS typically delivers multiparameter data — such as fluorescence brightness, lifetime, and spectra — of molecular- or nanometre-scale particles such as single dye molecules, quantum dots, or fluorescently labelled biological macromolecules.

arxiv-2501-13207.title: Beyond MESA Defaults: The Impact of Structural Resolution Uncertainty in p p -mode Asteroseismology
arxiv-2501-13207.creator: Yaguang Li (李亚光) ⋆, Meridith Joyce ⋆
arxiv-2501-13207.description: Abstract Observations of pressure modes ( p p -modes) in stars have enabled profound insights into stellar properties, and theoretical stellar evolution and oscillation models are integral to these inferences. However, modeling uncertainties are often overlooked, even as they can rival or exceed observational uncertainties.

arxiv-2504-02051.title: Self-Resource Allocation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
arxiv-2504-02051.creator: Alfonso Amayuelas, Jingbo Yang, Saaket Agashe, Ashwin Nagarajan, Antonis Antoniades, Xin Eric Wang, William Wang
arxiv-2504-02051.description: Abstract With the development of LLMs as agents, there is a growing interest in connecting multiple agents into multi-agent systems to solve tasks concurrently, focusing on their role in task assignment and coordination. This paper explores how LLMs can effectively allocate computational tasks among multiple agents, considering factors such as cost, efficiency, and performance.

pmc-12365238.description: Khon Kaen Geopark (KKGp), located in the Western margin of the Khorat Plateau (Northeastern Thailand), showcases a complex topographic and structural framework shaped by regional tectonics. pmc-13085531.title: Single-stage concomitant extended thymectomy for myasthenia gravis and enucleation of a left recurrent laryngeal nerve schwannoma via median sternotomy
pmc-13085531.creator: Go Kamimura, Koki Maeda, Masaya Aoki, Satomi Imamura, Shoichiro Morizono, Yuto Nonaka, Aya Takeda, Toshiyuki Nagata, Kazuhiro Ueda
pmc-13085531.description: BackgroundMyasthenia gravis (MG) without thymoma is often treated with extended thymectomy to improve symptom control and reduce immunotherapy requirements. Schwannoma of the recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) is rare, and surgical resection is usually curative. However, operative manipulation carries a risk of temporary or permanent vocal fold paralysis. When these conditions coexist, choosing staged versus single-stage surgery is non-trivial.

pmc-13401250.description: INTRODUCTIONHealth professionals play a critical role in tobacco prevention and cessation, but limited training during education often leaves their knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and organizational support insufficient.
